direct: A high shoulder, a back descending toward the hips, a domed head, small ears, a short tail, a full coat, one trunk, two upper tusks, four limbs, and broad feet are evidence-led identity cues.
Mammuthus primigenius is a Cenozoic proboscidean in Elephantidae, not a dinosaur, mastodon, or modern elephant species.
analytical: The accepted body proportions combine skeletal and preserved-soft-tissue evidence across specimens; the exact silhouette of any pictured individual remains a reconstruction.
A vegetated cold dry mammoth-steppe is evidence-led at biome level, while the exact plants, frost, snow, weather, and local horizon are scene reconstructions.
hypothetical: Exact coat color, guard-hair placement, undercoat tone, sex, age, weather, movement, and the adult-calf relationship shown are hypothetical.
The mother-calf ecology image illustrates plausible proximity and plant gathering but is not a documented individual event.
mammuthus-primigenius.coatColorBoundary: Dark chocolate and charcoal umber are conservative gallery choices, not recovered color portraits. Bright blond or orange is not presented as the species default.
mammuthus-primigenius.softTissueBoundary: Do not add a separate camel-like fat hump. Preserve the skeletal high shoulder and descending back while treating precise trunk, ear, tail, foot-pad, and coat contours as reconstruction.
mammuthus-primigenius.behaviorBoundary: Maternal proximity and foraging posture are plausible comparison-based hypotheses, not direct observations of the pictured animals.
mammuthus-primigenius.habitatBoundary: The gallery uses forb- and grass-rich cold dry steppe-tundra with only patchy shallow snow, not an endless barren glacier.
mammuthus-primigenius.realmBoundary: Cenozoic / Quaternary / Pleistocene; a proboscidean mammal, not a dinosaur or Mesozoic animal.
